tasks.title: S2 sidecar: multi-language Tree-sitter loader + AST/CFG builder
acceptance_criteria: Loads Tree-sitter grammars for Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, C#, and SQL without network at runtime (via tree-sitter-languages OR per-language wheels: tree_sitter_python, tree_sitter_javascript, tree_sitter_typescript, tree_sitter_c_sharp, tree_sitter_sql)
Exposes `select_grammar(path: str) -> Language` which auto-selects by file extension: .py -> python, .js/.mjs/.cjs -> javascript, .ts -> typescript, .tsx -> tsx, .cs -> csharp, .sql -> sql
Defines a typed exception `UnsupportedLanguageError(extension: str)` and raises it (no silent fallback) for any extension not in the supported set
Exposes `parse_source(path: str, src: str) -> tree_sitter.Tree` returning a valid tree (root node populated) for every supported language

Exposes `build_call_graph(tree, src, language: str) -> dict[str, set[str]]` mapping function/method name -> set of called names within the module; works for all 5 languages (use language-specific node-type queries; SQL graph maps procedure/function names to invoked CALL/EXEC targets, statement-level if no functions defined)
Handles syntax errors gracefully per language: returns empty graph + parse_ok=False rather than raising
Module is importable as `from src.s2_core import parse_source, build_call_graph, select_grammar, UnsupportedLanguageError`
tasks.test_plan: Covered by RC-009. Unit-level: each of the 5 languages has a 2-function fixture where A calls B; build_call_graph returns {'A': {'B'}, 'B': set()}. SQL fixture uses CREATE PROCEDURE A() that CALLs B(). UnsupportedLanguageError raised for `.rb` and `.cpp`.
tasks.notes: tree-sitter-languages bundles compiled grammars for ~40 languages and is the path of least friction. Per-language wheels are second choice. Document chosen approach inline. TypeScript needs both `typescript` and `tsx` languages. | LEAD-FIX: SQL fixture migrated to PostgreSQL dialect — tree-sitter-sql 0.3 parses cleanly. 41 pytest pass.

tasks.title: S2 sidecar: ImpactReport scoring engine with real Mamba SSM forward pass
acceptance_criteria: Defines a typed `ImpactReport` (dataclass or pydantic) with fields: architectural_impact_score:float, coherence_delta:float, risk_vector:list[float] (len 8), regression_detected:bool, human_summary:str
Implements `score_change(path: str, before_src: str, after_src: str) -> ImpactReport`

Loads a real pretrained SSM checkpoint via `transformers.AutoModel.from_pretrained('state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf')` (or compatible — e.g. mamba2 variant — documented in ARCHITECTURE.md); model and tokenizer are cached in a module-level singleton so the load happens once per process

AIS forward pass executes a real `model(input_ids).last_hidden_state` reduction (mean-pool over sequence dim) on tokenized AST-derived text from before_src and after_src; coherence_delta is the L2 distance between the two pooled vectors (NOT a hashed n-gram fallback)
Forward pass runs on CPU by default; honors `S2_DEVICE=cuda` env var to opt into GPU
AIS is in [0.0, 1.0] derived from cosine similarity of the two pooled embeddings (1.0 == identical, clamped)

risk_vector has 8 dims labeled cyclomatic, fan_in, fan_out, depth, churn, coupling, cohesion, novelty (in this order); each dim normalized to [0,1]; novelty is derived from the Mamba embedding distance, the rest from AST/CFG metrics
regression_detected == True iff (AIS < 0.4) OR (coherence_delta > 1.5) OR any risk dim > 0.9
Scoring is deterministic given same inputs: model.eval() + torch.no_grad() + fixed seed; two calls with identical input produce bit-identical risk_vector and AIS
human_summary is non-empty and references the dominant risk dim when regression detected
First-call latency <= 30s on a cold model load (CPU); subsequent calls <= 3s on CPU for inputs <= 2KB
tasks.test_plan: Covered by RC-009. Determinism asserted by calling score_change twice on identical input and comparing all fields bit-for-bit. Latency budget asserted on the second call.
tasks.notes: RISK: Mamba inference on CPU may exceed the 5s sidecar timeout used by the hook (see RC-006). Mitigation options: (a) pre-warm the model in start-sidecar.sh and reuse the singleton, (b) bump hook timeout to 30s, (c) use mamba-130m (smallest published) — surfaced in board notes for lead decision.
qa_findings: BLOCKED (2026-05-01 QA pass 2): state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf and all fallback checkpoints failed to resolve from HF in QA environment (no cache, no network). All 6 score_change/determinism/embed tests skip cleanly. Static review of src/s2_core.score_change and src/ssm_backbone.embed confirms real Mamba forward-pass path via transformers.AutoModel + last_hidden_state mean-pool. Grammar wheels now installed (RC-003 partial) but SQL fixture fails -- does not affect this task. Lead to run huggingface-cli download state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf then rerun pytest to close.

tasks.title: Real SSM backbone: Mamba weight loader + tokenizer + AST-token bridge
acceptance_criteria: Exposes `load_backbone(checkpoint: str = 'state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf', device: str = 'cpu') -> tuple[PreTrainedModel, PreTrainedTokenizer]` that uses `transformers.AutoModel.from_pretrained` and `AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained` (trust_remote_code permitted only if the chosen checkpoint requires it; document in ARCHITECTURE.md)
Backbone is loaded once per process via an LRU/singleton; subsequent calls return the cached instance
Exposes `embed(text: str) -> torch.Tensor` returning a 1D pooled embedding (mean-pool over last_hidden_state seq dim) computed under torch.no_grad() with model.eval()
Honors `S2_DEVICE` env var (cpu | cuda); defaults to cpu
Honors `S2_SSM_CHECKPOINT` env var to override the default checkpoint string (so QA/lead can swap to mamba-370m or a future slide-mamba release)
Provides `ast_to_tokens(tree, src) -> str` that serializes the AST into a deterministic linearized string suitable for the SSM tokenizer (e.g. node-type + identifier sequence)

Module exposes a `BACKBONE_INFO` dict with keys {checkpoint, hidden_size, num_parameters, license, source_url} populated from the loaded model — consumed by ARCHITECTURE.md generation and /health endpoint
First-call latency budget: <= 30s on CPU for a cold load of mamba-130m; subsequent embed() calls <= 1.5s for inputs <= 2KB

If `transformers` cannot resolve the checkpoint (offline + no cache), raises a typed `BackboneUnavailableError` with a remediation hint (point user at `huggingface-cli download state-spaces/mamba-130m-hf`)

tasks.title: Plan-time guard: pre_plan_guard.py heuristic + SSM novelty scoring
acceptance_criteria: Hook reads Claude Code PreToolUse JSON payload from stdin and is invoked when tool_name is 'Write' AND tool_input.file_path matches one of: thoughts/shared/plans/**/*.md, **/PLAN.md, **/*.plan.md (case-insensitive). For non-matching paths it exits 0 immediately without scoring.

Heuristic checks implemented in src/plan_heuristics.py and unit-tested independently: (a) per-file LOC budget where any single file in the plan that is described as receiving > 400 LOC of new content emits a warning; (b) phase/file ratio where if the plan declares more 'Phase'/'Step' headings than distinct file paths the structure is flagged as too-broad-too-thin; (c) boundary-crossing detection scans for prose tokens like 'across', 'every file', 'all modules', 'global rename' and counts unique top-level dir prefixes in mentioned paths -- > 3 distinct top-level dirs flags 'boundary-crossing'.

SSM novelty score: extract every Markdown code fence block, concatenate, embed via src.ssm_backbone.embed; compute cosine distance against an embedding of a sampled cross-section (10 random files) of the existing repo. novelty = 1 - max(cos, 0). Score > 0.7 emits a warning.

Output is structured JSON written to stderr (one object per warning, fields: severity ['info','warn','block'], rule_id, message, file_path|null, span|null) plus a human-readable trailing summary line. Exit 0 by default; when env RC_PLAN_BLOCK=1 is set and any warning has severity == 'block' (currently only the per-file LOC > 800 case), exit 2.
If src.ssm_backbone.embed raises BackboneUnavailableError the hook still runs heuristic checks and emits a single 'novelty_unavailable' info-severity record; never raises uncaught.

Unit tests in tests/test_pre_plan_guard.py cover: (1) happy path -- balanced plan emits zero warn/block records; (2) over-budget single file -- 1200 LOC budget for one path emits severity=block under RC_PLAN_BLOCK=1, exit 2; (3) phase-to-file ratio 5 phases / 2 files emits warn; (4) boundary-crossing language across 4 top-level dirs emits warn; (5) high-novelty fenced code emits warn; (6) BackboneUnavailableError handled cleanly with exit 0; (7) non-plan path bypasses entirely with exit 0.
Hook latency budget: <= 5s on a 200-line plan when backbone unavailable, <= 12s when backbone forward pass runs (mamba-130m CPU).
tasks.test_plan: QA runs `pytest -q tests/test_pre_plan_guard.py`. Pipes synthetic plan-Markdown payloads representing each acceptance scenario. Captures exit codes and stderr JSON.
tasks.notes: Plan-time scoring is the missing-left-shift item from HARDENING.md residual gaps section. Heuristics are deliberately conservative -- a future task can tune thresholds against EVAL_DESIGN data. Threshold for 'block' severity (per-file 800 LOC) is intentionally high so default behavior never blocks Claude on plan creation.

tasks.title: Subagent inheritance audit + Task PreToolUse guard injection
acceptance_criteria: src/hooks/pre_task_guard.py reads the Task PreToolUse payload from stdin (tool_name == 'Task'), extracts tool_input.prompt and tool_input.subagent_type, and screens the prompt for verbs that indicate code mutation: 'implement', 'edit', 'write', 'modify', 'refactor', 'create', 'delete', 'patch'. Detection is regex-based, word-boundary aware, case-insensitive.

When mutation verbs are detected AND the prompt mentions any of the GUARDED_PATHS from pre_edit_guard.py (resolve same constant via shared import), the hook exits 2 with a stderr message naming the offending path token and verb. When env RC_ALLOW_SUBAGENT_GUARD_EDIT=1 the hook exits 0 with a warning instead.
When mutation verbs detected on non-guarded paths, the hook exits 0 but emits a stderr advisory naming the verbs detected -- this is informational and never blocks.
settings.json registers a PreToolUse entry with matcher 'Task' that runs `python3 ${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR}/src/hooks/pre_task_guard.py`, timeout 5000ms.

docs/HARDENING.md gets a new subsection 'L4 -- Subagent inheritance' describing the actual residual gap (subagents inherit settings.json from the parent project dir, so their tool calls DO pass through the parent hooks; the gap is only when the subagent's working dir is outside CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR -- documented with a concrete reproduction recipe and the screening fallback).

Unit tests in tests/test_pre_task_guard.py: (1) safe research prompt exits 0 silently; (2) 'implement edits to src/s2_core.py' prompt exits 2; (3) 'review the auth code' (no mutation verb) exits 0; (4) RC_ALLOW_SUBAGENT_GUARD_EDIT=1 downgrades block to warn; (5) malformed payload exits 0 with stderr note.
tasks.test_plan: pytest -q tests/test_pre_task_guard.py. Manual end-to-end: spawn a Task subagent with a payload that mentions src/s2_core.py and 'implement', verify it is rejected before the subagent boots.
tasks.notes: The user's brief says 'audit + fix'. After investigation: Claude Code DOES propagate settings.json to spawned Task subagents when they run in CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. The realistic residual gap is prompt-level intent screening, which this hook adds as a belt-and-braces layer. Documented openly in HARDENING.md so the gap is not silently papered over.

tasks.title: Persistent JSONL audit trail in sidecar (per-event records, redaction, ring buffer)
acceptance_criteria: src/audit_log.py exposes append_event(event: dict) -> None which writes a single JSON line to /tmp/rc-events/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<session_id>.jsonl. session_id is read from the env var CLAUDE_SESSION_ID (Claude Code-set) with fallback to a stable uuid-per-process hash. Directory created with mkdir -p semantics.

Every hook (pre_edit_guard, pre_bash_guard, pre_task_guard, pre_plan_guard) emits exactly one record per invocation with mandatory fields: ts (ISO-8601 with timezone), session_id, project_dir (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR), tool_name, file_path|command (exclusive), language, decision ('allow'|'block'|'warn'|'degraded'), ais|null, coherence_delta|null, regression_detected|null, latency_ms, before_bytes|null, after_bytes|null, retry_after_block|null.

Redaction rule: any file_path matching the patterns *secret*, *credential*, *.env, *.pem, *.key (case-insensitive on basename) has the file_path field replaced with the literal '[REDACTED]' before write. Bash command field has the same redaction applied to any token matching those patterns. Test fixture proves a path '/x/.env.production' becomes '[REDACTED]'.

Sidecar exposes GET /metrics returning JSON {p50_score_latency_ms, p95_score_latency_ms, sample_size, regression_rate, fail_open_count} computed over a ring buffer of the last 1000 /score calls. Ring buffer is in-process memory only (no persistence); reset on sidecar restart. Latency tracked with monotonic_ns precision.
Append is best-effort: if /tmp is unwritable the audit call logs a warning to stderr and returns silently -- never raises into the hook, never blocks the user.

Unit tests in tests/test_audit_log.py cover: (1) record schema validates; (2) redaction triggers on the documented filename patterns; (3) directory rotates by date when ts crosses midnight; (4) /metrics returns p50/p95 from a stubbed buffer of known latencies (deterministic percentile assertion); (5) /tmp-unwritable path degrades silently.
tasks.test_plan: pytest -q tests/test_audit_log.py. Manual: run a 30s session with multiple edits and verify the JSONL file accumulates lines with the right schema.
tasks.notes: Closes the instrumentation gap referenced at the bottom of HARDENING.md. Ring buffer is intentionally in-memory; persisting it is a follow-up. Redaction list is conservative -- expand once the team sees real false-positive misses in the trail.

tasks.title: Cumulative repo-baseline drift: session-level embedding + new regression rule
acceptance_criteria: src/repo_baseline.py exposes set_baseline(repo_root: str) -> None and current_baseline() -> Optional[torch.Tensor]. set_baseline walks the repo (respecting .gitignore via subprocess `git ls-files`), samples up to 100 files (deterministic random with seed 0), embeds each via src.ssm_backbone.embed, and stores the mean-pooled embedding in a module-level singleton.
Sidecar exposes POST /baseline with body {repo_root: str} that calls set_baseline and returns 200 {status: 'ok', n_files_sampled: int, hidden_size: int}. POST with bad body returns 400.

score_change extended: when current_baseline() is not None, also computes cumulative_drift = ||embed(after_src) - baseline||_2 and includes it in the ImpactReport (new field). Default ImpactReport.cumulative_drift is None when no baseline set.

New regression rule: regression_detected becomes True if any of the existing conditions OR (cumulative_drift is not None AND cumulative_drift > 3.0). The 3.0 threshold is documented in ARCHITECTURE.md (new subsection 'Cumulative Drift Calibration') and chosen as 2x the mean intra-repo embedding distance from a 1000-file calibration sample.
ImpactReport JSON serialization adds the new field; existing consumers (mcp_reasoner, hooks) tolerate both old (no field) and new (field present) shapes.
Sidecar startup honors env RC_BASELINE_ROOT -- if set, calls set_baseline(RC_BASELINE_ROOT) after the SSM is loaded, before binding the HTTP listener.

Unit tests in tests/test_repo_baseline.py: (1) set_baseline on a tmp git repo with 5 files succeeds and current_baseline() returns a tensor of shape [hidden_size]; (2) score_change against an in-baseline file yields cumulative_drift << 3.0 and regression_detected reflects only the per-file rules; (3) score_change against an unrelated text file yields cumulative_drift > 3.0 and regression_detected==True; (4) /baseline POST end-to-end via TestClient; (5) ImpactReport schema test asserts cumulative_drift field present with float|None type.
tasks.test_plan: pytest -q tests/test_repo_baseline.py. Manual: start sidecar with RC_BASELINE_ROOT=/Users/jakubsikora/Repos/personal/reasoning-core, verify /health reports baseline_loaded:true.
tasks.notes: Threshold 3.0 is a placeholder pending RC-217 calibration on real eval data. The Data Eng cross-verification flagged that raw L2 thresholds are checkpoint-dependent (item 3 in the suspicious-items list); this task knowingly inherits that risk and is gated by the eval suite to retune.

tasks.title: Eval toolkit: per-task harness run_task.sh
acceptance_criteria: run_task.sh signature: `eval/run_task.sh <task_id> <arm>` where arm in {'vanilla','treatment'}. Sets `set -euo pipefail`, exits non-zero on missing args or unknown arm.
Looks up task metadata from eval/datasets/swe_bench_verified_python_subset.json (jq parse). Clones repo at base_commit into /tmp/reasoning-core-eval/<task_id>/<arm>/repo (fresh per arm).
If arm == treatment: starts the sidecar via scripts/start-sidecar.sh in background, polls /health up to 60s, captures pid for teardown. If arm == vanilla: skips sidecar entirely.

Invokes Claude via the `claude` CLI with --model claude-opus-4-7, temperature 0, max-turns 40, system prompt from eval/prompts/system_prompt.txt; treatment passes the project settings.json (so hooks fire); vanilla passes --no-hooks. Captures stdin from a generated problem statement file (PROBLEM.md derived from task fail_to_pass tests + repo README).

After Claude exits: runs `python -m pytest <gold tests> --tb=no -q --timeout=60` in the repo to populate test_results.json (gold_tests_passing: bool, newly_failing_tests: [str], pre_existing_failures: [str]).

Writes per_task_metrics.json with: {task_id, arm, gold_tests_passing, regression_detected, wall_clock_seconds, hook_blocks: int|null, hook_fail_opens: int|null, input_tokens, output_tokens, novelty_drift_mean: float|null, claude_exit_code, timeout: bool}.
Tears down: SIGTERM the sidecar if started, rm -rf the scratch repo dir on success (preserve on failure for debugging).
When env var RC_LIVE!=1, the script enters dry-run mode: prints the would-be commands and the resolved task metadata, exits 0 without invoking Claude or pytest. This makes CI smoke tests safe.
Tests in tests/test_run_task.py: (1) bash -n run_task.sh; (2) shellcheck clean; (3) dry-run on a real task_id prints the expected jq-resolved fields.
tasks.test_plan: Run `eval/run_task.sh django__django-11099 vanilla` in dry-run mode and inspect the printed plan. Run shellcheck. pytest tests/test_run_task.py.
tasks.notes: claude CLI invocation specifics may differ across Claude Code versions; use the published `claude --help` flags as of 2026-05. If --no-hooks is unavailable, use SETTINGS_DIR pointed at an empty directory for the vanilla arm. Document the exact flag in the script header so the harness is self-describing.

tasks.title: Eval toolkit: suite runner run_suite.py with paired task scheduling
acceptance_criteria: CLI: `eval/run_suite.py --n N --arms vanilla,treatment [--dataset PATH] [--out DIR] [--parallel K] [--seed S]`. N defaults to 5 (smoke), dataset defaults to eval/datasets/swe_bench_verified_python_subset.json, out defaults to eval/results, parallel defaults to 1, seed defaults to 42.

Selects the first N tasks from the dataset after deterministic shuffle by seed. Runs both arms for each task. With parallel > 1, uses concurrent.futures.ProcessPoolExecutor to run K task-arm pairs concurrently (each pair still sequential -- vanilla then treatment for a given task to share a pre-warmed scratch).

For each (task, arm), invokes eval/run_task.sh as a subprocess with a wall-clock cap (default 1800s per arm; configurable via --task-timeout). On timeout, kills the process group and writes a per_task_metrics.json with timeout=true.
Writes a top-level eval/results/run_summary.json {schema_version, started_at, finished_at, n_tasks, arms_run, dataset_sha, runtime_seconds, completed: int, timed_out: int, errored: int}.

Honors RC_LIVE: when unset, run_suite.py prints the planned schedule (which tasks and arms in which order) and exits 0 without spawning run_task.sh. CI uses this dry-run mode by default; smoke runs gate behind RC_LIVE=1.
Logs to stdout in human format and to eval/results/run_suite.log in JSONL (one record per task-arm transition).

Unit tests in tests/test_run_suite.py: (1) --help exits 0 and lists all flags; (2) dry-run schedule matches expected ordering (deterministic given seed); (3) bad arm name exits non-zero; (4) parallel=2 schedule contains the documented interleaving.
tasks.test_plan: pytest tests/test_run_suite.py. Manual: `python3 eval/run_suite.py --n 5 --arms vanilla,treatment` (dry-run) prints the schedule.
tasks.notes: Concurrency primitive is process-pool (not thread-pool) so each runner gets its own sidecar instance. The sidecar binds 127.0.0.1:8765 -- if parallel>1 in treatment arm, conflicts will occur; mitigation is to bind sidecar on a port chosen from a per-task offset (8765 + worker_id). Document this and gate parallel>1 behind treatment-only when sidecar port allocation lands.

tasks.title: Eval toolkit: aggregate.py with paired stats + 10-metric report
acceptance_criteria: CLI: `eval/aggregate.py --results-dir DIR --out report.json [--format json|markdown|both]`. Default both: writes report.json + report.md side by side.
Loads every per_task_metrics.json under DIR and joins on (task_id) across vanilla and treatment arms, also joins the JSONL audit trail from /tmp/rc-events/ for hook event counts and decisions.

Computes all 10 metrics from EVAL_DESIGN.md: Regression Rate (RR), Resolved Rate (ResR), AST Edit Distance (AED), Cyclomatic Delta (CycΔ), Fan-In/Fan-Out Delta (FIOΔ), Hook FPBR, Hook TPBR, Block-Recovery Rate (BRR), Wall-clock Latency (Latency_task), Hook overhead p50/p95 (HookOverhead), Token cost (Tokens), Novelty Drift (NovΔ). Each metric reports paired difference mean, BCa 95% CI (10000 resamples via scipy.stats.bootstrap), Wilcoxon signed-rank p, Holm-corrected p.

Decision-criteria block in report.md applies the EVAL_DESIGN section 7 thresholds (RR delta >=0.15, ResR no worse than -5pp, FPBR<=0.10, latency ratio<=1.5, BRR>=0.60) and prints PASS/FAIL per criterion, plus an overall ship/kill/inconclusive verdict.

Handles missing tasks: any task that errored or timed out is included with documented imputation (RR=0.5, novelty=NaN excluded from mean). The report distinguishes 'completed', 'errored', 'timed_out' counts in a header section.

Tests in tests/test_aggregate.py: (1) given a fixture results dir with 5 fake task pairs, aggregate produces a valid report.json schema; (2) Wilcoxon p computed against scipy.stats matches; (3) Holm correction matches statsmodels.multitest.multipletests; (4) decision block correctly flips on synthetic data crafted to fail criterion 1; (5) markdown rendering does not crash on edge cases (n=1, all-zero diffs).
tasks.test_plan: pytest tests/test_aggregate.py. Manual: build a 2-task fixture results dir and run aggregate -> inspect report.md.
tasks.notes: Adds scipy + statsmodels to requirements.txt -- both are heavy. Keep the import lazy (only loaded when aggregate runs) to keep the hook path fast. Holm correction over 10 metrics will eat statistical power on n=5 smoke runs -- the smoke output is descriptive only; ship/kill verdicts only meaningful at n>=50.

tasks.title: Eval toolkit: AST/cyclomatic helper scripts (ast_edit_distance, cyclomatic_delta)
acceptance_criteria: ast_edit_distance.py CLI: `<gold_patch_path> <claude_patch_path>` -- parses both as unified diffs, applies each to a synthesized base file, computes ast.dump on each side, returns integer count of node insertions+deletions via difflib.SequenceMatcher over the dumped representations.
